records.text: Jerri Frantzve was awarded a gender research center at Radford University in 1983
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Back to Dr. Jerri (Jerri Frantzve), she is then somehow awarded an entire clinic, research center, pardon me, at Radford University in 1983, a gender clinic of all things.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. Radford's Center for Gender Studies history says organizing began in 1989-90, lists Jerri among participating faculty, and identifies Hilary Lips—not Jerri—as director; this contradicts a 1983 award/directorship.

sources.title: History of the Center for Gender Studies at Radford University
sources.relevance: Center history dates formation to 1989-90, lists Jerri as faculty, and names Hilary Lips as director.

records.text: A Radford University report coauthored by Jerri Frantzve included her mother Marjorie Weiland among the listed authors without disclosing the family relationship
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Jerri Frantzve. Well, not what she doesn't communicate in this report is that that's her family. Marjorie Wayland is her mom.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. The report's catalog record supports that Jerri Frantzve and Marjorie Weiland were coauthors, but no reliable source located establishes that Weiland was Jerri's mother or that disclosure was legally or academically required.

sources.title: Emerging Female Leaders Within the Closed Societies of American Indian and Appalachian Artisans
sources.relevance: ERIC copy lists Jerri Frantzve and Marjorie Weiland as coauthors.

sources.title: Marjorie Weiland Obituary
sources.relevance: Obituary identifies Jerri Frantzve as Marjorie Weiland's daughter.

records.text: Richard Castor, another author of Jerri Frantzve’s Radford report, was her nephew
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Richard Castor is her nephew, her sister's son. This is why they just get married so much because and I didn't even look into the other two.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. The report identifies Richard Castor as a coauthor, but current sources did not independently establish the alleged nephew relationship.

records.text: Jerri Frantzve married at age 14, later became a psychologist, created the Tesseract model, and received a gender research center at Radford University.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: At the age of 14, married by the age of 14, a bookie turned psychologist, creator of the Tesseract model, Radford University, gave her a research center, a gender research center.

verification.notes: Radford's archive confirms Jerri Frantzve was a psychology professor and co-founded the Center for Gender Studies in 1989. Live research did not find reliable public evidence for the age-14 marriage or that she created the Tesseract model; 'received a center' is also imprecise because the archive describes her as a co-founder.

sources.title: Center for Gender Studies Collection RU 3.4 | Radford University Archives
sources.relevance: Confirms Frantzve was a Radford psychology professor and co-founded the Center for Gender Studies in 1989.
